target.title: fix(memory-wiki): honor memory_search deadline during wiki exhaustive scan
target.body:
Closes #104719

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running `memory_search` with `corpus="wiki"` or `corpus="all"` against a large compiled-wiki vault would hit `memory_search timed out after 15s` when digest-selected candidates underfilled `maxResults`. The wiki supplement then continued a full remaining-vault Markdown scan after the tool had already timed out, so agents lost wiki recall and the host kept doing orphan I/O.

## Why This Change Was Made

The memory tool already owns a fixed deadline (`AbortSignal`), but the corpus-supplement bridge never forwarded it into memory-wiki search. Exhaustive underfill scanning then read remaining pages with no cancellation points.

This PR threads an optional `signal` through `MemoryCorpusSupplement.search` → wiki corpus supplement → `searchMemoryWiki` / `searchWikiCorpus`, and makes page reads batch-aware so an aborted deadline returns partial results and stops further file I/O.

Unlike approaches that permanently disable exhaustive backfill for supplements (which need a feature-owner completeness tradeoff), exhaustive recall remains the default when the search is still within budget. Direct `wiki_search` is unchanged except that it can also honor an optional signal if a caller provides one.

## User Impact

Agents using compiled-wiki supplements through `memory_search` no longer leave large orphan vault scans running after a tool timeout. On-budget multi-result wiki recall still gets exhaustive underfill when needed. Operators avoid multi-second post-timeout host work on large vaults.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (Crabbox bypass)

Closeout notes:
- `pnpm check:changed` ran >1h on local `tsgo:extensions` / `tsgo:extensions:test` without a clean exit; stopped per 1h non-convergence policy.
- Substitute: focused Vitest for the fixed surface + `oxfmt` on the 8 touched files + `git diff --check` (clean).

Focused tests (all pass):

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  extensions/memory-wiki/src/corpus-supplement.test.ts \
  extensions/memory-wiki/src/query.test.ts \
  extensions/memory-core/src/tools.citations.test.ts
# Test Files  3 passed (3)
# Tests  74 passed (74)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-wiki/src/query.test.ts -t "104719"
# Tests  3 passed | 41 skipped (44)
```

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: memory-wiki exhaustive underfill ignored the memory_search deadline; host work continued after the tool timed out.
- Environment: local macOS arm64, openclaw checkout at `ff333ee80`, Node via repo Vitest harness (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`).
- Current-main contrast: `searchMemoryCorpusSupplements` did not accept/forward an AbortSignal; `searchWikiCorpus` underfill listed and read every remaining Markdown path with no abort checks (`extensions/memory-wiki/src/query.ts` exhaustive path).
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-wiki/src/query.test.ts -t "104719"`
  2. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-core/src/tools.citations.test.ts -t "forwards effective agent context"`
- Evidence after fix (redacted transcript):
  ```text
  ✓ returns no wiki hits when the caller deadline is already aborted (#104719)
  ✓ still exhaustively finds body-only hits when the deadline is not aborted (#104719)
  ✓ stops mid-scan when the deadline aborts during exhaustive page reads (#104719)
  ✓ forwards effective agent context to memory_search corpus=wiki supplements
     (expects signal: AbortSignal)
  ✓ forwards effective agent context to memory_search corpus=all supplements
     (expects signal: AbortSignal)
  ```
- Control check: on-budget exhaustive underfill still finds a body-only page outside digest candidates (`still exhaustively finds body-only hits…`). Pre-aborted search returns `[]` without scanning. memory_search tool tests assert the deadline signal is forwarded into the supplement API.
- Observed result after fix: deadline-aborted wiki search stops/returns partial; non-aborted search retains complete exhaustive underfill; memory_search passes `deadlineSignal` into supplements.
- What was not tested: live 77 MB / 1,220-file vault timing on a real Gateway (issue’s large-vault numbers); permanent digest-only supplement mode (intentionally not chosen — preserves completeness when within budget).

## Linked PR context

Open PR #104793 targets the same issue with deadline propagation **plus** `exhaustiveFallback: false` for supplements. ClawSweeper on that PR asked for feature-owner approval of digest-only completeness tradeoff and stronger query-level tests. This PR follows the safer half of that guidance: signal propagation + abort-aware I/O without changing on-budget recall completeness.

## AI disclosure

This fix was authored with AI assistance (Grok / xAI contributor agent). Human operator requested an automated find→fix→PR pipeline; proof is local Vitest transcripts above.

target.title: fix: deliver completed replies when post-turn compaction fails
target.body:
Closes #94688

Related: #94928

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users could lose a completed channel reply when post-turn transcript compaction failed or the gateway restarted during compaction. The reply could already be present in the local transcript and Control UI while never reaching the originating channel.

## Why This Change Was Made

The turn owner now records the canonical, user-visible pending final before optional post-turn compaction. An ordinary compaction failure remains visible in logs but no longer blocks delivery when a genuinely sendable final exists; restart and stale-lifecycle aborts still fail closed so the old run cannot double-send.

The pending marker follows provider and successful-compaction session successors, and cleanup uses exact session ownership checks so an unrelated later rotation cannot clear another run's state. Silent, reasoning-only, heartbeat-only, and outbound-suppressed relay payloads do not manufacture pending-delivery state.

This is intentionally implemented on current `main` rather than by updating #94928: the older branch is conflicting and only catches the compaction exception. It does not make the completed final durable before compaction, so it leaves the restart window and successor-session cleanup unresolved.

## User Impact

Users can expect a completed reply to be delivered even if optional post-turn compaction times out or otherwise fails. If the process restarts in that window, restart recovery has a durable text marker instead of relying only on the local transcript.

No configuration surface or timeout default changes. Empty or intentionally suppressed replies still treat compaction failure as fatal, and successful compaction behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Validation environment: local macOS using the repository's narrow Codex-worktree fallback; hosted CI is pending on this draft.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-command.compaction-rotation.test.ts` — 15/15 passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/pending-final-delivery.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/reply-utils.test.ts src/infra/outbound/payloads.test.ts` — 122/122 passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` — passed.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/agents/agent-command.ts src/agents/agent-command.compaction-rotation.test.ts` — passed.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/agents/agent-command.ts src/agents/agent-command.compaction-rotation.test.ts` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Regression coverage verifies CLI and embedded replies, compaction-successor adoption, failed-delivery retention, restart/stale lifecycle ownership, and suppression of empty, `NO_REPLY`, reasoning-only, heartbeat-only, and relay-status payloads.
- No live configuration was changed and no private transcript or deployment log is included in this PR.

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted investigation, implementation, test authoring, and review. I inspected the changed lifecycle, delivery normalization, session-store/restart-recovery paths, and the sibling Codex app-server compaction contract, understand the resulting behavior, and addressed all findings from local `codex review --base origin/main` before opening this draft.
